answer: Submission rate is limited to 5 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole swarm from one uplink. An operator running many aliases hence pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the mesa quota and the lagoon admission check. Because the counters live in the pearl ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
